newsitem.title: GERMANY: Linotype works council slams Kiel centralisation.
newsitem.headline: Linotype works council slams Kiel centralisation.

text.p: The works council of the German printing systems maker Linotype-Hell AG said on Monday that it did not agree with the decision by the board to centralise all activities at is Kiel production site.

The decision to concentrate all activities in Kiel is part of a company revamp following its takeover earlier this year by the printing machinery group Heidelberger Druck AG, a subsidiary of Rheinelektra.

The works council said Linotype's Eschborn plant, near Frankfurt, was being sacrificed to pay for years of management mistakes and that concentrating group activities in Kiel would lead to a loss of know-how and cause logistical disadvantages.

On Friday Linotype said it would make a loss of about 70 million marks in 1996 and would cut 1,200 of around 3,300 jobs at the company as part of a major restructuring to be completed by the end of 1997.
Shares in Linotype were down four marks at 120 marks in late bourse trade in Frankfurt on Monday, off earlier lows of 115 marks.
